note: 'Through Him all things were made' (John 1:3) against 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.' (Gen 1:1). One says created and the other made, so the tie is by sense rather than by word -- but Gen 1:26 uses make, and John 1:3 leaves nothing out of its scope.
'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.' (Gen 1:1).
'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.' (John 1:1).

'In the beginning was the Word' (John 1:1); 'In the beginning God created' (Gen 1:1). The first three words are identical and John gives no citation formula, so the graph asserts the echo and not a quotation. It is the plainest verbal tie between the two chapters and everything else here follows it.

The Word is made flesh at v14 and the chapter names Jesus Christ at v17 without a break in the subject. John never writes the identity as a sentence, so the graph makes the join.; 'and His name is The Word of God.' (Rev 19:13).
'He separated the light from the darkness' (Gen 1:4).
'Let there be light,” and there was light.' (Gen 1:3).

'He gave the right to become children of God' (John 1:12). John does not use the word adoption and Paul does not use this phrase; both describe becoming sons by gift rather than by birth, and Rom 8:15 says so in one word. The graph's join.
'The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.' (John 1:5).
'that life was the light of men' (John 1:4).

'The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.' (John 1:5) takes up the two things Gen 1:2-4 puts first, in the same order. Genesis divides them; John has one shine in the other and reports the result. Neither passage refers to the other.
'And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.' (Gen 1:2).
'The true Light, who gives light to everyone' (John 1:9) and 'I am the light of the world' (John 8:12) -- the same claim in the same gospel, once about him and once by him.
'We have seen His glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father' (John 1:14).
